A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpatialViz-Bench with the same 1,180-item, 12-task design. The complete main texts and Appendices A–F, including algorithms, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations in Tables 2–7, a human baseline in Figure 1, and qualitative analyses of model responses.

after.justification: V4 retains original benchmark evaluations and additionally reports non-CoT evaluations, quantitative error analysis and detailed human accuracies.

M1.justification: All 21 generation algorithms match across versions. Task-construction descriptions move from Section 4.2 to Appendix B.1; the programmatic-generation terminology and dynamic-test-bank emphasis do not establish a new generation procedure. CoT controls concern evaluation of existing models.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 12 tasks, difficulty levels and 1,180 examples, including DeepCAD projections and 80 manually designed Mechanical System questions. The added prompting and error analyses reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparison falls from 33 to 27 models, omitting Gemini-1.5-pro, both LLaVA-OneVision variants and three InternVL2.5 variants. The five open-source models remain in Appendix E.1; Gemini-1.5-pro is removed from those detailed comparisons too. Human rows are added to tables, although a human baseline already appeared in v1 Figure 1.

E3.justification: V1 evaluates models under one zero-shot CoT regime. V4 adds direct-answering controls for eligible models, with explicit prompting and exclusion rules, plus a four-model, multi-label error-review protocol using two annotators and Gemini assistance. Expanded human-study details do not establish that the existing study changed or was rerun.

E4.justification: V4 adds a CoT-versus-non-CoT ablation and a six-category error analysis across four models, substantially extending v1's difficulty breakdowns and Gemini case studies. The earlier difficulty analysis is retained unchanged; Figure 5 primarily condenses existing appendix cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports model seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, dispersion or formal significance tests. V4's statistical error analysis adds descriptive frequencies without uncertainty estimates or annotator-agreement statistics.

E6.justification: Matched CoT scores remain unchanged, including Gemini-2.5-pro at 44.66% and o1 at 41.36%. V4 adds non-CoT results, such as Kimi-VL-A3B-Instruct at 32.37% alongside its retained 23.90% CoT score, difficulty-level human results and error frequencies. Some previous comparison rows disappear. Exact new error totals remain unclear because Figure 4 and Section 5.3.1 give different counts.

T1.justification: The mathematical operations and cube-count bounds in Appendix B remain unchanged, as does Section 3's cognitive framework. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations are introduced; the new error categories are operational descriptions.

C1.justification: V4 introduces CoT-induced accuracy degradation as a headline finding and explicitly claims a first comprehensive framework and contamination prevention through dynamic test-bank updates. The benchmark and spatial-deficit claims remain. V1's difficulty-mismatch, 2D-to-3D and formula-use findings persist in the later body and appendix despite losing abstract prominence.

C2.justification: V4 adds explanations that compulsory reasoning text can interfere with visual judgment and that scaling alone does not resolve core spatial deficits. It extends the pretraining-bias discussion to analytical versus simulative internal world models. Appendix F explicitly bounds the study to intrinsic abilities and leaves tool-assisted evaluation to future work.

D1.justification: V4 supplies the non-CoT prompt, human recruitment and sampling details—eight participants and 72 problems each—mechanical-question authoring and verification roles, and error-label definitions. It also documents option distributions and corrects several illustrated answer keys in Appendix C. These disclosures do not establish regenerated benchmark data; hardware, model-version listings and access links are retained.

R1.justification: The central positioning against perception/memory benchmarks and narrowly focused visualization tests remains. V4 adds contamination, benchmark-survey and DeepSeek-R1 references, explicitly credits CLEVR's generation approach, and cites Blender/FreeCAD. It removes the broader world-knowledge/domain-benchmark survey and several model references; SRBench is the previously cited Stogiannidis work.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contributions and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten. Detailed task construction moves into Appendix B.1, while evaluation is reorganized into main results, prompting ablation, statistical error analysis and case studies. These are substantial structural changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V4 redraws and combines overview material, redesigns the generation diagram, and replaces Table 1 with task/objective/distractor/difficulty columns. The main result tables merge with new prompting columns and human rows. New error charts and a collage of existing appendix cases substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The non-CoT control reveals prompting sensitivity that v1 did not test, while fuller human-study documentation and corrected illustrated answers improve transparency. These provide a limited net gain. However, the new diagnostic evidence has unexplained totals: Figure 4 gives o1/Qwen-72B counts of 312/284, versus 236/272 in Section 5.3.1. Its claim that scaling nearly eliminates memory/calculation errors is also unsupported by Figure 4, limiting the improvement.
